newsitem.title: USA: FORD JULY N. AMERICAN OUTPUT RISES 12.6 PCT.
newsitem.headline: FORD JULY N. AMERICAN OUTPUT RISES 12.6 PCT.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. said Wednesday it produced 241,157 cars and trucks in North America during July, a 12.6 percent increase over the 214,115 vehicles it built in July 1996.

Ford said its July passenger car production in the United States, Canada and Mexico totaled 99,134 units, a 6.9 percent decline from the 106,503 cars produced a year earlier. Ford's North American truck production for the month totaled 142,023 units, 32 percent higher than the 107,612 units built in July 1996.

Ford said its U.S. production in July rose to 204,897 cars and trucks from 178,889 a year ago, while Canadian production dropped to 20,263 vehicles from 23,005 a year ago. July output of Ford vehicles in Mexico rose to 15,997 from 12,221 a year ago.
Year to date, Ford said it has produced a total of 2,542,895 vehicles in North America, up 1.6 percent from the 2,503,521 units it built during the first seven months of 1996.

Ford said on Tuesday it plans to add 30,000 vehicles -- split evenly between cars and trucks -- to its third quarter North American production schedule. With the extra units, Ford now intends to produce 988,000 vehicles during the July-September period, including 393,000 cars and 595,000 trucks.
